name: Moped
description: A seated vehicle on no more than three wheels with an automatic drive whose power source can't push it past 30 mph on level ground; an electric motor of any wattage qualifies, since the 50 cc limit applies only to combustion engines. An electric two-wheeler that tops the limits of an electric assisted bicycle and of a motor assisted scooter but can't exceed 30 mph is a moped. Defined by Oregon Revised Statutes §801.345.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, no more than three wheels on the ground, and a power drive system that needs no clutching or shifting
Its power source can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground; the statute sets no wattage limit for an electric motor
Riders need a driver's license of any class, so must be 16 or older; no motorcycle endorsement
Riders must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet
Titled and registered with the DMV, with a license plate, and must carry liability insurance
Kept off sidewalks and bicycle paths, and allowed in a bicycle lane beside the roadway only while pedaled
One that can go faster than 30 mph is a motorcycle and needs a motorcycle endorsement
